chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhayna, from Bureyd al-Ijali, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) regarding the words of God, Mighty and Majestic:
'But rather, you are only a warner, and for every people is a guide' [Quran 13:7]

So he said: 'The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) is the warner, and for every era there is a guide from us who guides them to what the Prophet of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) came with. Then the guides after him — Ali, then the successors, one after another.'

key_terms.أَوْصِيَاء: Successors (Awsiya') — the Imams designated as heirs of the Prophet's mission
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — an honorific for God
key_terms.مُنْذِر: Warner — the Prophet's role in warning humanity
key_terms.هَادٍ: Guide (Imam) — the divinely appointed leader for each era

ai.seo_question: What does Quran 13:7 mean according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) interprets the Quranic verse 13:7, which states that the Prophet is a warner and every people has a guide. The Imam explains this as a clear proof of the doctrine of Imamate: the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) is the eternal warner, while each era has a designated guide (Imam) from the Ahl al-Bayt, beginning with Ali and continuing through the successive Imams. This teaching was given to Bureyd al-Ijali, a trusted companion, establishing the theological foundation for the perpetual guidance of the Imams.
